                        </ns0:gap>,</ns0:hi> were consumed: God by their Sin was so grieved with them after such ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />perience of his Power for so long a time. See <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 32.10. <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 14.22.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 Wherefore I was grieved with that ge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />neration <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Because they thus tempted and proved him by hard<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ning their hearts in unbelief<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Forty Years, God the Redeem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />er, <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 63.16. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 10.9. <ns0:hi>was grieved,</ns0:hi> is attributed to him improperly, who is not subject to Passions, but as Men grown impatient with grievous and oppressive Burdens; so <ns0:hi>He</ns0:hi> expresseth his dislike, disdain of them, and resolution to bear no longer, as <ns0:hi>Amos</ns0:hi> 2.13. They split on him, as a Ship on a sharp point of a Rock, so as God hath loss, offence and trouble by it; and all of them did so carry it to Him the whole Age of them but <ns0:hi>Caleb</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ioshua, Psal.</ns0:hi> 95.10.</ns0:note>, and said, They do alway err in <ns0:hi>their</ns0:hi> hearts <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">They follow Deceit and Lying in their Doctrine and Wor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ship with all their Heart, so that it is diffused through their Persons, and that seat of Truth is made depth of Error, to the stupifying of their Hearts even to very madness, and this was their state all their time.</ns0:note>, and they have not known my ways <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Notwithstanding God's Works were among them and his Word, yet they would not know his Mind, so as to approve, love, and walk in God's ways. His Law, Doctrine, revealed Truth and Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mands were all cast behind their Back, <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 23.35.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:549" />11 So I sware in my wrath <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Such was their Provocations and Temptations of their Redeemer, that he determined their Punishment; the cer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tainty of which he fixt by an irreversible Oath, which is the highest confirmation of Vengeance when it cometh from Wrath; as of his Promise when it issueth from Grace, <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 14.27, 28, to 36. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 95.11. compar'd <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 6.17, 18. And the Spring of it here is Wrath, inraged by their Murmurings and Unbelief.</ns0:note>: <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Gr. <ns0:hi>If they shall enter.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> They shall not enter into my rest <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">The Punishment is exprest in an expostulatory form, which is vehemently asserting the negative of the Question; <ns0:hi>They shall never enter into my Rest. If they enter in,</ns0:hi> then I am neither True nor God. The Rest literal was the Land of <ns0:hi>Canaan, Deut.</ns0:hi> 12.9. in the Truth of that Type, <ns0:hi>Heaven.</ns0:hi> It is the Redeemer who speaks this, whose Rest it is by way of Efficiency, Purchase, and Dona<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion; he gives entrance into it, and shuts out of it, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 7.21, 22, 23. This is a shutting them out of all Peace, in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to Eternal Sorrow, Anguish, Distress and Trouble, and eve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry other Evil contrary unto this Rest.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 Take heed Brethren <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Here the Spirit applieth the former dreadful example of Sin and Judgment to the <ns0:hi>Hebrews,</ns0:hi> to forewarn them how they sinned as these did, lest they partake of the like Vengeance, and so enters his Caution against Unbelief. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> signifies not an act of Sight, but of the Mind, <ns0:hi>Cir<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cumspection,</ns0:hi> Watchfulness, and Heed, taking exactest caution of the Evil forbidden, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 12.15, 25. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 8.9. Brethren they were to <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> in the Flesh, and more so as True Belie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vers in Christ, he cautions them particularly, one by one, lest any Root of Bitterness should be amongst them, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 12.15.</ns0:note>, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Heart</ns0:hi> is the first, and proper, and chiefest subject wherein all Sin riseth, and from thence issueth into Words and Works, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 15.18, 19. compare <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> 1.14, 15. This comprehendeth the Mind, Will and Affections, the whole in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ward Man; and this Heart in every Man is naturally and ha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bitually Evil, continually forging and framing of it, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 6.5. compare <ns0:hi>Ierem.</ns0:hi> 17.9. Almighty Grace only can change this Heart, yet it works by Counsel, and makes the Soul willing to use the means appointed to effect it. <ns0:hi>VNBELIEF,</ns0:hi> though but in it self, is but a denial to assent to, or rely on the Will of God revealed to it, yet is the Spring and Fountain of all other Sin, the teeming Womb from whence all issueth, as, Uncleanness, Idolatry, Unrighteousness, Su<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />perstition, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> It was the hardening Sin of their fore-fathers, they would not Believe, and then did Murmur and Rebel: It is the root of Apostacy; Men breaking their Co<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />venant with God in Christ, do then desert him: Against this Persidious, Impious, perverted Temper doth he caution them to watch, that neither for <ns0:hi>measure</ns0:hi> nor <ns0:hi>season</ns0:hi> they ever do admit or allow it; that there be not at all in the least degree, or at any time such a base, malignant quality in their Hearts, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 11.20, 21.</ns0:note> in departing from the living God <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Turning away, standing off, and separating the Heart,</ns0:hi> it implies in it a real, total, final defection; actual and formal Apostacy from him whom they had owned and received, and is actual Rebellion against their lawful Soveraign, by turning either Jews or Heathens, and renouncing the Christian Religion and its Author, who is <ns0:hi>the Living God,</ns0:hi> not only <ns0:hi>formally</ns0:hi> as opposed to dead Idols, but efficiently the Author and Fountain of all sorts of Life, but especially of Spiritual and Eternal Life, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 5.19, 20, 21, 25, 26. which Living God is our Lord Jesus Christ, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 7. whose Voice they were to hear, who was tempted by their Unbelief in the Wilderness, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 10.9. who gave the Law to them at <ns0:hi>Sinai, chap.</ns0:hi> 12.26. So that to apostatize from him and his Religion, is to apostatize from God, and to renounce Eternal Life, and to subject themselves to Eter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nal Punishments, which he <ns0:hi>ever liveth</ns0:hi> to inflict on them; Unless they took heed to avoid this Unbelief, it was im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />possible for them to persevere in Christianity, when threat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ned with Persecutions, and the loss of Peace, Liberty, Safety, Estates, Honours, Relations, and Life it self for it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 But exhort one another daily, whilst it is called, To day <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">The means to avoid the former Evil, is, to <ns0:hi>Exhort,</ns0:hi> which as a private Duty, is an earnest, frequent calling on, stirring up, or perswading, incouraging to perseverance in the Christian Religion, and to put away all Heart-Evil, espe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cially Unbelief, which traineth to Apostacy; to which are subservient God's Precepts, Promises, Threatnings suitably applied by them: And this is not only privately, but es<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pecially publickly, by the regular Ministration of the Word and Ordinances to the whole Society of Christians, as they are personally obliged to it, being Members one of another, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 12.25, 27. And this they are to do <ns0:hi>instantly,</ns0:hi> for no Man is sure what may be on the Morrow, he being but a Days-Man, living, and supplied, as working by the day; sufficient to the day is the Duty as well as the Evil in it, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 6.11, 34. Whilst then the day of Grace and Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pentance lasts, in which God calls and intreats, and will hear and help, the opportune time of exhorting, the ve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry instant wherein God expecteth it, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 7. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 95.7. And every one as thus to look to another, must begin with himself, lest any miscarry; Charity, especially as to this, should begin in every Christian at home.</ns0:note>, lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Lest themselves or others, refuse the Gospel rendred, or reject and apostatize from it after professing it, so as to become not only obsti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nate, but rebellious by Unbelief, and an habitual hardned Heart; so as the sinful, natural habit of our Soul, <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> 1.12.15. So horrible vile in it self, that were it not masked, Nature would abhor it, might be drawn forth by the false Colours, as the Devil blinds Sin with, to delude the Under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />standing, and to catch and insnare the malignant Will, that it swallows it more and more, to the hardning of the Heart; That Divine Promises, Threatnings, nor Admonitions can make any impression; it being unmoved under the appli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cation of all these, disregards the Christian Faith, and hath its issue in a total Apostacy, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 17.9. <ns0:hi>Ephes.</ns0:hi> 4.22. 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 1.19.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 For we are made partakers of Christ <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>For,</ns0:hi> shews this to be a rational motive, urging home the former Counsel, unto which the following Condition doth agree; for we Believing Christians and Brethren are made <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, <ns0:hi>Partners</ns0:hi> with the Primitive Proprietor supposed in it, even <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> who hath of his own the fulness of God, Life, Grace, Glory, and all good; in all which fulness of his we share, by virtue of our Union with him, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.16. <ns0:hi>Ephes.</ns0:hi> 1.22, 23. <ns0:hi>Col.</ns0:hi> 1.19. and 2.9, 10. And he by his Spirit will free us from the deceitfulness of Sin, and hard<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ning by it.</ns0:note>, if we hold the beginning of our confidence <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">If by a Spiritual <ns0:hi>tenaciousness,</ns0:hi> and firm fix<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing in our hearts, we hold <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, either the <ns0:hi>principal</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>fundamental</ns0:hi> Truth, as the word signifieth in Sciences; or, the <ns0:hi>entrance or beginning</ns0:hi> of our Course, as used in things, so as the first step in Christianity is stiled a beginning of Grace.</ns0:note> sted<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fast unto the end <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, in personal relations is, a <ns0:hi>real subsist<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ence,</ns0:hi> as of the Son in the Trinity, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 1.3. <ns0:hi>In things,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Basis</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Foundation</ns0:hi> upholding others, and this in Christia<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nity is Christ principally, who bears up his Church, <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 2.20, 21, 22. And Faith the Instrument, whereby we receive Christ, is so called, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 11.1. That which renders present and subsisting what is hoped for to the Soul; so that here it imports the retaining firm that Principle of Truth, up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on which Christians are bottomed and supported to Life, that is, Christ himself, and the true Doctrine of him; as also, that we must firmly stand in the first beginnings of Faith, and encrease in them, so as they may be firmly fixed in our Hearts, and our Hearts on them, so as never to be removed as long as we live; our retaining firmly of this, makes us partners in Christ; both <ns0:hi>instrumentally</ns0:hi> helping in it, and <ns0:hi>evi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dentially</ns0:hi>; It being the infallible consequence of true Grace, holding us to this Communion with Christ. How ought these Conditions to quicken the activity of Believers.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 Whilst it is said, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ver. 7.</ns0:note> To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts, as in the provocation <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">This is another circumstance of the Example of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> applied to them: That since <ns0:hi>now</ns0:hi> Christ is speaking to you, as he did to your fore-Fathers then; the same Voice concerneth you both, so, as not to morrow, or when you will, but <ns0:hi>To day,</ns0:hi> if you will believe what God speaketh to you by him, and hath recorded in his Word concerning his being the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> and render not your selves deaf to God's Voice, or obdurate through Unbelief, as your fore-Fathers did, when their Unbelief and hardness of Heart imbitter'd God's Spirit against them, because acting in it against their solemn Vows and Engagements to him, so as to Apostatize from him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 For some, when they had heard, did pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />voke <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">This is a rational enforcement of the former Duty pressed, it being as possible for them to provoke Christ as others, they should look to it, and not harden their hearts; for the greater <ns0:hi>some,</ns0:hi> the most of the Congregation of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> imbittered God's Spirit by their Unbelief and hardness of Heart; though Christ spake to them from Heaven, as never was before done, and daily by <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> they were hearing Counsels by which they might live, yet provoked they him, and would not believe.</ns0:note>: howbeit not all that came out of Egypt by Moses <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">This rightly interprets the Psal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mist, and sets a better example of their Fathers for them to follow: Let <ns0:hi>Caleb</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ioshua,</ns0:hi> Believers, and Obedient to God, be your Patterns to imitate; He aggravates the Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />obedience of the one, and the Obedience of the other. They all had equally a clear Exemption and Deliverance from the place of Bondage, and that by <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> by whom God wrought such Miracles as might command Faith from any; yet these <ns0:hi>some,</ns0:hi> by murmuring and striving with the Redeemer, provoked him: how great is their Sin? How suitable and pleasing the Obedience of the others to him?</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:549" />17 But with whom was he grieved forty years <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">By these Questions, the Spirit makes a more lively re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />presentation of these unbelieving provokers of God, that his Reason may have the more force with them; <ns0:hi>Do ye observe with whom God was grieved?</ns0:hi> the form puts them on more exact notice for their caution: God suffers not by Passion, but these redeemed out of <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi> carried it contrary to him, and crost his Will, that which usually grieveth us. Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerning the Word, see <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 10. It is used by the <ns0:hi>Septuagint, Deut.</ns0:hi> 7.26. to express that detestation and abhorrence which <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> was to shew against Idols, that they should be a <ns0:hi>grief</ns0:hi> to their Soul not to be indured: <ns0:hi>Idols</ns0:hi> are cal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />led <ns0:hi>Grievances</ns0:hi>; he was displeased and grieved with their Covenant-breaking with him Forty Years together. These Sinners by their Unbelief, Murmuring, Idolatry, Rebellion against his Officers and Ordinances, and their other Lusts, so imbitter'd his Spirit, that he by various Judgments destroy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed and turned them into the Grave and Hell together, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 10.5, to 11. <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> and others of God's own cannot be numbred among these Sinners, for their Sins were pardon<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed, and Persons accepted; and though they came short of the literal, had a much more abundant entrance administred to them into the Heavenly <ns0:hi>Canaan.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>? <ns0:hi>was it</ns0:hi> not with them that had sinned, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Num. 14.22, 29, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>

                     </ns0:gap> 5.</ns0:note> whose carcases fell in the wilderness <ns0:hi>s</ns0:hi>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 1.34, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">To prevent these <ns0:hi>Hebrews</ns0:hi> falling, the Spirit repeats the direful Oath of God to Apostates in the Wilderness. The form of which was opened, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 11. compare <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 14.30. The matter sworn was, that they should be so far from possessing, that they should not as much as enter into the Land of Promise, <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> which was God's Property, as the whole Earth is; he promised it to them, could only dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />possess their Enemies, did give it in Possession to their Seed, and made it a Type of Heaven, and of his Rest there; he swore this in his severe vindictive Justice, so as his Sen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tence was irreversible: which Oath stands good against all total and final Apostates from him, who have thereby for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />feited any Title to God's Eternal Rest.</ns0:note>, but to them that be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieved not <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Those who were unbelieving under all God's Miracles of Mercies and Judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ments, which they saw, and so became obstinately disobe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dient to God's Commands, and broke his Covenant, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 8.9. <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 31.32. and apostatized from him, and so perished in their gain-saying.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 So we see they could not enter in, because of unbelief <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">The execution of the matter sworn was felt by these <ns0:hi>Hebrews,</ns0:hi> which should make them and all that read it, to dread both their Sin and Punishment, which the Gospel would as justly inflict on them, if Unbelievers. It is to be seen in God's written Record of it, and the experienced downfall of such, that God's Oath had shut the Door as to their entrance there, and his Judgments consumed them in the Wilderness; because of their denial of resting on God's Word, and the impious practices that issued from it, in their rejecting Promises, rebelling against Precepts, and murmuring against Providence. God is no respecter of Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons; if we sin so against his Son and Gospel, how much sorer Punishment will overtake us? <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 10.27, 29.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
